 Dated this the 12th day of January, 2023
 Judgment

This writ petition is filed with following prayers:
i. To issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate directing the 4th respondent to pass award in respect of the property acquired for the 2nd respondent in compliance with Exhibit-P6 judgment and pay compensation or in alternative to issue a necessary direction to the respondents to measure the property of the petitioner on the basis of the survey records and give back possession of the property in the original position as on the date of taking possession.

ii. To initiate necessary legal proceedings against the 4th respondent for not complying with the directions in Exhibit-P6 judgment and recover an amount of 1 lakh towards compensation to the petitioner for mental agony and loss caused to the petitioner.
iii. To grant such other relief's as this Honourable Court may deem fit in the circumstances of the case.

(SIC)
2.
This writ petition is filed for issuing a direction to the 4th respondent to pass an award in respect of the property acquired for the 2nd respondent in compliance with Ext.P6 judgment.
Short facts are like this: Petitioner is the owner of 31  cents of land in Survey No.1254 and 2 cents of land in Survey No.1206 of Peroorkada Village in Thiruvananthapuram District.
The Government published a notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act on 05.03.1998 for taking over the land for the purpose of implementing Sewerage Main Project.
On the basis of the request made by the requisition authorities, it is the case of the petitioner that the property was given in advance possession on 25.03.1998.
The total extent surrendered, according to the petitioner, is 2.25 cents of land.
The respondents published Section 6 declaration on 22.06.2000.
It is the case of the petitioner that her property is item Nos.1 and 8 in the notification.
Thereafter, according to the petitioner, the District Collector passed award in several cases and most of the land owners obtained the award amount also.
But the petitioner and some other persons did not receive the award amount.

It is the further case of the petitioner that on enquiry it has come to the knowledge of the petitioner that there is scarcity of the funds and that is the reason of non disbursement of the award amount.
The copy of the award is also not received.

Subsequently the petitioner filed WP(C) No.23410 of 2008 before this Court seeking a direction to the respondents to disburse the amount of compensation for S.Geethakumari vs State Of Kerala on 12 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79365187/
2 the land acquired as per Ext.P3 notification and for a direction to the respondents to measure the property of the petitioner on the basis of survey records and give back possession of the property in the original position in case it is found that no award is passed.

This Court as per Ext.P6 judgment,
directed the respondents to negotiate with the petitioner and settle the issue regarding the correct compensation payable for the petitioner's acquired property within two months of receiving copy of the judgment and also observed that if negotiated settlement is not possible, the 2nd respondent will deposit the amounts called for by the 4th respondent.
It is also directed to pass an award in respect of property actually taken over from the petitioner's possession.
The case of the petitioner is that flouting the directions of this Court in Ext.P6, Ext.P13 is issued.
Hence this writ petition.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader.
I also heard the learned Standing Counsel for Kerala Water Authority.

4. The counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is aggrieved by the compensation fixed by the requisition authority and the petitioner want to refer the matter to the court under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act.
Ext.P12 is the application.
The counsel submitted that no award is passed consequent to Ext.P6 judgment and instead of that, Ext.P13 communication is issued in violation of Ext.P6 judgment.

The Government Pleader, on the other hand, takes me through paragraphs 3 and 4 of the counter affidavit filed by the 4th respondent and submitted that there is no violation of the directions issued by this Court in Ext.P6 judgment and as per the Land Acquisition Act, the award can be passed only in accordance to Section 11A of the Land Acquisition Act.
The Standing Counsel for Water Authority submitted that the issue was already reported to the Land Acquisition Authority and the land was taken advance possession.
The amount of compensation was already deposited before the Land Acquisition Authority.
5. This Court considered the contentions of the petitioner and the respondents.
This Court perused Ext.P6 judgment and Ext.P13 communication issued by the Special Tahsildar to the petitioner.
I am of the considered opinion that Ext.P13 communication itself is flouting the directions issued by this Court in Ext.P6 judgment.
It will be better to extract the relevant portion of Ext.P6 judgment:
"2. Under the above circumstances, I am of the view that there is no escape to the respondents from the obligation of passing award and paying compensation.

I dispose of the writ petition issuing the following direction;
The second respondent and higher officials of the Kerala Water Authority are directed to negotiate with the petitioner and settle the issue regarding the correct compensation payable for the petitioners acquired properties within a period of two months of receiving copy of this judgment.

If such negotiated settlement is not possible, the second respondent will deposit the amounts called for by the fourth respondent with that respondent within six weeks from the expiry of the period of two months referred to above.

Upon deposits being made by the second respondent as directed above, the fourth respondent will not delay matters further and will pass award in respect of the property actually taken over from the petitioner's possession so that the petitioner can receive the compensation.

It is made clear that since S.Geethakumari vs State Of Kerala on 12 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79365187/
3 possession has already been taken, the proceedings have not lapsed.

sentences.text:
If the fourth respondent finds that there is controversy between the requisitioning authority and the petitioner regarding the extent, the fourth respondent will hear the petitioner as well as the second respondent and then only take a decision as to the correct extent acquired from the petitioner."
[underline supplied]
6. The Government Pleader argued based on paragraphs 3 and 4 of the counter affidavit filed by the 4 th respondent.
The same is extracted hereunder:
"3. It is submitted that the publication of declaration is not the completion of acquisition.

After issuing declaration Under Section 6 of LA Act the LAO will fixing the value of compensation and will issue statutory notice Under Section 9(3) and 12/2) to the land owners inviting the filing of documentary evidence to prove their title.

The petitioner and other land owners were not issued with 9(3) notice and 12(2)
notice.

In this case before issuing statutory notice or request by the LAO the land owners and KWA avoided the LAO and the land owners had voluntarily and freely surrendered the land for construction of road and sewer line without expecting any compensation.

It is submitted that the petitioner was filed a WP (C) No. 24310/2008 before the Honourable High Court of Kerala allegedthat her property was taken possession by the Kerala Water Authority for laying sewer line and the compensation has not paid even surrender her property to the Kerala Water Authority.

The Honourable High Court of Kerala directed on 23.10.2008 to the Kerala Water Authority to negotiate with the petitioner and settle the issue of compensation or the Special Tahsildar will disbursed the compensation to the petitioner.

Accordingly the Kerala Water Authority handed over an amount of Rs.80.801/- to the Special Tahsildar and the Special Tahsildar has been disbursed the same amount to the petitioner by way of compensation on 21.05.2011.
It is true that the LAO handed over the compensation fixed by the KWA to the petitioner based on the judgment in WPC 23410/08.

The Award is not passed and the LA become denova under Section11 (A)
of LA Act.
Therefore the compensation fixed by the KWA has been handed over to the petitioner.
4. The Special Tahsildar was issued a 'D' form cheque and not a chalan to the petitioner.
The 'D' form cheque included the compensation fixed by the KWA to the petitioner.
The request under Section 18 of LA Act of the petitioner not be considered since no award is passed under section 11(1) of LA Act.
The LAO is not aware about the mutual understanding between the landowners and the KWA.
The LAO did not request the land owners to surrender the property in advance to the KWA.
The Kerala Water Authority did not provide money to the LAO for passing the Award.
The LAO did not grab the land of the petitioner.
The land owners were directly dealing with the KWA by avoiding the LAO.

The LAO is not known whether the S.Geethakumari vs State Of Kerala on 12 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79365187/
4 petitioner and the KWA had changed the alignment of the project.
The land owners had voluntarily and freely surrendered the property to the Kerala Water Authority without any request made by the LAO."
7. I am of the definite opinion that the affidavit filed by the 4th respondent itself is flouting the directions issued by this Court in Ext.P6 judgment.

In Ext.P6 judgment this Court clearly stated that, the Water Authority is directed to negotiate with the petitioner and settle the issue regarding the correct compensation payable for the petitioner's acquired property.

If such negotiation is not possible, it is also stated that the 2 nd respondent in that writ petition, the Executive Engineer,
Severage Project Division will deposit the amount called for by the 4th respondent within six weeks.

Upon deposit being made by the 2nd respondent in that writ petition, this Court also directed the 4th respondent to pass award in respect of the property actually taken over from the petitioner's possession so that the petitioner can receive the compensation.
This Court also made it clear that since the possession has already been taken the proceedings have not lapsed.

When this Court without any ambiguity stated that the land acquisition proceedings will not be lapsed and when there is a direction to pass an award, the Land Acquisition Officer cannot take a stand that, if the award is passed, that will be against the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act.
If the Land Acquisition Authorities are aggrieved by Ext.P6, their remedy is to file a review petition or to challenge that judgment.
As long as Ext.P6 judgment and the directions in it are in force, it is the bounden duty of the Land Acquisition Authorities to follow the same and pass award.
According to me, the contentions of the Land Acquisition Authority in paragraphs 3 and 4 of the counter affidavit is to be rejected.
There can be a direction to the Land Acquisition Authorities to comply with the directions in Ext.P6 judgment in letter and spirit.

If no award can be passed as per the Land Acquisition Act because that Act is lapsed, the Land Acquisition Authorities are free to proceed as per the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text:
Therefore, this writ petition is allowed in the following manner:
1. Ext.P8 communication is set aside.

2. The Land Acquisition Authorities are directed to proceed as per the directions in Ext.P6 judgment and take appropriate steps to pass the award in accordance to law,
as expeditiously as possible, at any rate, within four months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

3. I make it clear that if no award can be passed under the repealed Land Acquisition Act, the Land Acquisition Authorities are free to proceed as per the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
